$comment: Flamingo City business listings. Generated from the sourced dossiers in /research. Read _meta before consuming.

_meta.source_of_truth: research/<city>/<slug>.md — each listing below traces to one dossier file

how_to_use.publication_status: Filter on this. 'ready' = every published field traces to a source and no blocking gap remains. 'needs_owner_confirmation' = publishable, but blocking_gaps lists what must be asked before the listing is complete. No listing here is unusable; they differ in how much is still open.
how_to_use.field_provenance: Fields carrying real risk (hours, price, owners, founding dates) are objects with a 'source' URL and, where sources disagree, a 'conflicts' array. Do not flatten a conflicts array by picking one silently.
how_to_use.seo.json_ld: Spec-valid schema.org object built ONLY from validated fields, ready to emit in a <script type="application/ld+json"> tag. Kept separate from the internal fields because schema.org has no way to express 'this claim is unverified'.
how_to_use.hours_policy: openingHoursSpecification is present in json_ld ONLY where an owned channel (the business's own site or its own Instagram bio) supplies a single unambiguous schedule. Where sources conflict it is omitted entirely rather than guessed, because wrong hours in structured data surface directly in Google and generate owner complaints.
how_to_use.founding_dates: corporate_record.filing_date is the date an entity was registered with Florida. It is NEVER an opening date and must never be rendered as 'since ____'. Where an opening or founding year is known it lives in its own 'established' field with its own source. Several businesses have no established year at all; those fields are null by design, not by omission.
how_to_use.privacy: Officer residential addresses appear in Florida corporate records but are deliberately excluded here. Owner names and titles only.
how_to_use.missing_values: Any field with the literal string "N/A" has no sourced value yet — it is a known gap, not an error. List-typed fields (owners, references, signature_items, cuisine, ...) stay as arrays and are EMPTY rather than "N/A", so iterating them is always safe. Each listing carries a 'missing_fields' array naming every gap on that record. seo.json_ld deliberately OMITS unknown fields rather than filling them with "N/A" — schema.org output goes to search engines, and a literal "N/A" in structured data would publish as real content.
how_to_use.uniform_keys: Every listing now carries an identical key set, so the site can render one template across all records without existence checks.
how_to_use.missing_fields: Lists only the CORE fields that are absent and worth chasing - identity, contact, hours, price, owners, corporate record. Optional blocks that simply do not apply to a given business (capacity, brand, awards, related_locations) are filled with "N/A" for template uniformity but are NOT counted here, so the number reflects real work outstanding rather than schema padding.

known_limitations: Research is web-only. No owner has been contacted. Each dossier's 'Ask the owner' section holds the open questions.
search.sunbiz.org, Yelp, Tripadvisor and the Herald sites block automated retrieval. Corporate fields sourced via aggregators are marked with verification: 'aggregator'.
No images are included. Each dossier lists candidate image URLs with provenance and a rights contact; licensing is unresolved and is the site owner's decision.

listings.short_description: Full-service Cuban restaurant on East 8th Avenue, open from 7am daily with a full bar and a name older than its owners.
listings.long_description: Molina's Ranch has been feeding East 8th Avenue since the early eighties, opening at seven every morning for breakfast and running through lunch and dinner with a full bar. Burger Beast traces its roots to Adolfo Molina in 1982, with longtime chef Jose Orlando taking over in 1994; today it is run by the Jorge family, with Jose Jorge as executive chef. The kitchen leans classic Cuban — croquetas, bistec artesano, guarapo pressed fresh, cafecito with espumita, and flan worth ordering.
caveats: The business contradicts itself on its own age: the Instagram bio says 'more then 40 years' while an August 2026 post advertises a 50-year anniversary. Unresolved — ask before publishing either.
Florida records show a separate Adolfo Molina corporation at 4100 E 8th Ave, one block over. Do not conflate the two addresses.
Your list called this 'Molina'. No Hialeah restaurant trades under that bare name.

listings.owners_note: The restaurant carries the Molina name but is operated by the Jorge family. Burger Beast attributes its 1982 beginnings to Adolfo Molina. How the business passed from the Molina name to the Jorge family is documented by no source located — do not narrate that transition.
